topSignals.title: Elcogen's "quiet streak" corrected — a Nov 2 MoU with electrolyser maker Hygreen Energy was missed by this monitor's prior daily checks; Elcogen is actually 13 days quiet, not 54+.
topSignals.text: Direct fetch of elcogen.com/category/news today turned up a Nov 2, 2026 item that trade press (QC Intelligence, paywalled beyond the lead) reported as an MoU to integrate Elcogen's solid oxide stack technology into Hygreen Energy's electrolyser (SOEC/hydrogen-production) portfolio. No capacity, funding, or timeline figures are disclosed in the available text. For Dominic: this is a correction, not breaking news — the item is now two weeks old — but it means Elcogen's real last-activity date is Nov 2, 2026, not the Sept 21 baseline this monitor carried through Nov 1-14; the "days quiet" counter restarts today at 13 days. QC Intelligence

items.text: Elcogen (priority) — CORRECTED: Not quiet since Sept 21 as previously tracked. A Nov 2, 2026 MoU with Hygreen Energy (electrolyser maker) to integrate Elcogen's solid oxide stack technology into Hygreen's electrolyser portfolio was found today via direct fetch of elcogen.com/category/news; it had been missed by this monitor's checks on Nov 3-14, likely because it surfaced only via a paywalled trade outlet (qcintel.com) rather than a general news search. No capacity/funding/timeline disclosed. 13 days quiet as of today (Nov 2 baseline). Status otherwise unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27, 2026 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via direct fetch of topsoe.com/press-releases today — 80 days quiet. Topsoe's press feed stays active but entirely non-solid-oxide: newest items are a Nov 12 Sasol e-SAF (Sweden) technology-selection and the already-logged Oct 29 HDF Energy/Texas "BaseBlue Power" blue-hydrogen-plus-PEM data-center project — neither is SOEC/SOFC.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (Ceres Power, Sunfire): no new item for either; results repeated Ceres' standing licensee roster (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai) and Sunfire's Schwarzheide SOEC test-facility background, both pre-dated.

Today's Tier 2 sweep plus Mitsubishi Power/Kyocera/Aisin check: no new item; recycled Kyocera/Mitsubishi Power/Aisin SEO-aggregator background and Bloom Energy/FuelCell Energy's standing AI-datacenter narrative.

Today's Tier 3 rotation — new cycle 10, round 1 (Reverion, Convion, Hexis, Doosan Fuel Cell, SK ecoplant, Watt Fuel Cell) plus an OxEon Energy/Nexceris/Weichai sweep: no new item for any; recycled the standing Doosan-Reverion $76.7-78M SOFC stack-supply background, Convion's HD Hyundai ownership, Hexis's dormant post-Viessmann status, SK ecoplant's Singapore SOFC data-center background, and Watt Fuel Cell's residential-only (non-data-center) WATT HOME product line.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP/Google Cheyenne Fuel Cell LLC (702 MW/$4B, 20-yr PPA, confirmed Google offtake), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). Also hosting a DOE/national-lab-backed R&D testbed (StabilityMax) in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
